title: PartitionDependency
description: A cross-field constraint in combinatorial test design stating that when a specific partition value (the trigger) is selected in one InputSpacePartition, the availability of named partition values in another input field is excluded, required, restricted, or re-ranged, so that generated combinations omit invalid inputs. Use PartitionValue instead when the condition bounds a single field's own equivalence class (its constraintExpression) and does not depend on the value chosen for any other field. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the restriction is a per-CoverageRequirement choice of which values of one partition to cover or exclude (coverValues/excludeValues), not a rule that applies whenever another field takes a given value. Use InputSpacePartition instead when you are describing the input dimension itself and its presenceRule (including a plain 'conditional' flag), rather than the specific trigger value and affected values that make it conditional. Use CoverageExclusion instead when a target or requirement is deliberately removed from coverage with an approver and accepted risk, rather than a combination being logically invalid.

dependsOnPartition.description: ID of the testing.inputspacepartition that triggers this dependency

dependsOnValue.description: Label or ID of the testing.partitionvalue that activates this dependency

effect.description: How the dependency affects the related partition values

affectedValues.description: Comma-separated labels or IDs of the partition values in the dependent field whose availability is modified by this dependency (e.g., values that are excluded, required, or restricted when the trigger value is selected).

description.description: Free-text explanation of the business or technical reason the trigger value constrains the affected values (e.g. 'guest accounts cannot hold admin role'); set whenever the rule is not self-evident from effect and affectedValues.

x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Level Test Design Specification (test design refinements: feature/input combinations to be tested); conceptually the category-partition method's selector constraints (Ostrand & Balcer)
x-dr-evidence: A constraint line in a combinatorial test model file, e.g. a PICT/ACTS model containing 'IF [PaymentMethod] = "invoice" THEN [Country] IN {"DE","AT"};'

A parametrized test generator (e.g. pytest_generate_tests, JUnit ArgumentsProvider, itertools.product filter) that drops or skips tuples when one parameter has a specific value and another has a listed value
A property-based test calling assume()/filter() that ties one generated argument's allowed values to another argument's value, e.g. 'assume(not (account_type == "guest" and role == "admin"))'
